answer: One practical defence is staking reputation to a scarce, verifiable history: an agent must complete many small, attested tasks before it can move large value, so spinning up fresh identities is slow and costly. Think of trust like a marble quarry — each block is earned one cut at a time, not conjured overnight. A newcomer starts on a short voyage of low-stakes work, and only after a lotus of consistent, checkable behaviour blooms does the network grant it real economic weight. Sybils stay cheap to create but expensive to make credible.
